text:
Alex: noticing a spike from the RDU POP starting ~22:12 UTC, p95 latency up ~3.2x and throughput dropped ~40% for short-token requests
Priya: seeing that on the dashboard too — p50 stable but p95 and p99 ballooning, any recent deploys?
Alex: no deploys at 22:00-22:15, conf checks clear. Kernel selector logs show a lot more 'fallback' kernel picks for short sequences
Jin: hmm, fallback picks correlate with kv-cache miss bursts? Can you paste the cache hit/miss numbers?
Alex: quick snapshot from metrics: 
```
time: 2026-03-18T22:11:30Z
pop: rdu
p50: 18ms
p95: 127ms (normally ~38ms)
throughput: 60rps (was 100rps)
kv_cache_miss_rate: 48% (normally ~6%)
kernel_selector_fallback_rate: 42% (normally <5%)
dns_rto_rate: 1.9% -> 7.4%
```
Mateo: DNS RTO increase + kv miss rate smells like upstream path/DNS issue causing delayed backend calls — if requests hit slower origin, kv warmups time out and we get more cold runs -> fallback kernels and batching noise
Kara: any change in our edge provider or new peering event in RDU earlier?
Luis: cloud-provider posted a partial BGP flap at 22:05 for RDU region, some routes diverted to a different transit for ~8m. I can share the incident link: https://status.cloud.example/incident/8234
Priya: that would explain increased round trip + some weird retransmits. But why kv cache miss jumps by 8x?
Alex: hypothesis: the runtime's short-sequence batching heuristic uses measured host latency to keep sessions warm. When RTT increases, rollout of aggressive batch formation gets delayed, causing many micro-requests to be treated as cold and miss KV prefix cache. Also kernel selector probes are timing out and choosing safer scalar path for correctness -> slower per-token
Jin: can we verify by pulling pprof traces from the POP? I saw some spikes in `runtime.cpusampler` and `kernel_selector` locks
Alex: pprof snapshot: https://perf.redwood/rdu/pprof/2150006789 (heatmap attached)
Mateo: grabbing logs now: `kubectl logs -n inference rdu-runtime-0 --since=15m | grep -E "kernel_selector|kvcache|dns"`
Mateo: logs show repeated `kernel_probe timeout` and `kvcache refresh failed: lookup error (i/o timeout)` entries
Kara: ops-bot deploy suggestion: roll the POP routing to the previous edge peer while cloud provider resolves BGP. Can we apply route-steer?
Luis: I opened a support ticket with provider, but we can try steering to alternate transit via our peering fabric. Requires a canary apply to routing table.
Priya: quick mitigation ideas: 1) reduce kernel probe timeout (so selector falls back less aggressively) 2) temporarily favor hot-kv policy (lower TTL for warm keys) 3) throttle batching heuristic to be less sensitive to transient RTTs
Alex: I'd prefer 2 + 3 for fastest rollout. Reducing probe timeout might make things worse if network is flaky. 3 is config-only: `BATCHER_SENSITIVITY=low` and `KV_WARM_TTL=60s`
Jin: prepping a PR for runtime flags: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4523 - will patch config and add a short-circuit to prefer hot-kv when RTO rate > 2%
Alex: can we try a targeted config flip on one instance first?
Kara: I'll trigger a canary: `/deploy-bot canary rdu-runtime config=hot-kv-ttl-60 batcher=low`
deploy-bot: Canary started for rdu-runtime (1/5 nodes) — monitoring p95 and kv miss rate
Mateo: after canary (2m): p95 down from 127ms -> 56ms, kv_miss 48% -> 22%, kernel_fallback_rate 42% -> 18%
Priya: good signal. Apply to remaining nodes?
SRE-Oncall: recommend waiting next 3m for stability but this looks promising. Also keep provider ticket open — steering alone won't fix all edge cases
Luis: continuing to push alternate peering. Provider says BGP convergence in progress, ETA 12-18m from incident start
Alex: after full rollout (22:28 UTC): p95 stabilized at ~34ms, throughput back to ~98rps, kv_miss back to ~7%
Kara: follow-up actions: 1) add detection rule for kv_miss_rate > 15% + dns_rto > 3% to auto-trigger reduced batching sensitivity 2) instrument kernel_selector probe latencies in local metrics 3) add runbook for routing-steer during provider BGP events
Jin: I'll open an infra ticket to add the detection rule and wire a PagerDuty playbook: https://tickets.redwood/infra/1289
Mateo: note for postmortem: kernel probe timeouts are a symptom, not root cause — root cause was cross-region routing changes at transit that increased DNS/latency and caused chain reaction in heuristics
Alex: agree. Postmortem draft in #postmortems after we collect logs and provider timeline. Thanks everyone for fast triage :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident logged as "RDU pop transient BGP/peering event causing kv-cache warmup regression" (INC-2026-0318-09)
Priya: adding retention for pprof traces for 72h
Luis: provider confirms convergence at 22:17 UTC and route stability at 22:22 UTC
Alex: closing thread once postmortem is posted. Moral: heuristics need to be resilient to short network path flaps and we should prefer kv-warm policies during noisy neighbor / peering degradations
